questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the zona orbicularis related to?
questions.explanation:
Zona orbicularis is related to the neck of femur. It consists of circular fibres of the capsule of the hip joint.

The hip capsule has two sets of fibres: circular fibres (zona orbicularis), which are internal and form a collar around the femoral neck and blend with pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments; and longitudinal fibres, which are external, are numerous anterosuperiorly and are joined by the iliofemoral ligament.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false about the ligaments of the hip joint?

options.text: Iliofemoral ligament is the strongest ligament of hip joint
Transverse acetabular ligament contains cartilage cells
Ischiofemoral fibers fuse with the zona orbicularis
Pubofemoral ligament is triangular in shape

questions.correctAnswerText: Transverse acetabular ligament contains cartilage cells
questions.explanation:
The false statement is that the transverse acetabular ligament contains cartilage cells. It crosses the acetabular notch and continues peripherally with the labrum.

Ligaments of the hip joint: iliofemoral ligament is the strongest; pubofemoral ligament is triangular; some ischiofemoral fibres fuse with zona orbicularis and inferior fibres attach to the posterior circumference of the femoral neck; the transverse acetabular ligament forms a foramen allowing vessels and nerves to enter the joint; the ligament of the head of femur has its apex attached to the fovea and base to the margins of the acetabular notch.

Source note: iliocapsularis lies immediately deep to the iliopsoas tendon and above the anterior hip capsule. Its function is unclear and is thought to taut the hip capsule to prevent impingement during hip flexion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 16-year-old gymnast was brought to the emergency department after suffering severe trauma during the performance. She presented with painful hip instability. MRI revealed ligament tear which is caused by hyperextension of the hip joint. Which of the following ligaments is likely to be torn?
questions.explanation:
The iliofemoral ligament resists hyperextension of the hip joint and is therefore likely to be injured.

The iliofemoral ligament (ligament of Bigelow) is the strongest ligament of the hip. It is an inverted-Y-shaped ligament; its apex is attached between the anterior inferior iliac spine and acetabular margin and its base attaches to the intertrochanteric line. It prevents hyperextension.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 30-year-old male presented with pain and stiffness of the right hip. Ultrasonography revealed effusion in the right hip joint. At which position of hip joint will the pain be minimal?
questions.explanation: A patient with hip-joint effusion has least pain in the flexed and abducted position. Joint capacity is maximal with the hip partially flexed and abducted, making this the position of greatest comfort.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Artery passing through the structure marked in the diagram below is a branch of:
questions.explanation:
The marked structure is the ligament of the head of femur. The artery passing through it is the foveal artery/artery of the ligament of the head of femur, derived from the acetabular branch of the obturator artery.

The femoral head also receives blood from the trochanteric arterial ring formed by medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries with minor contributions from superior and inferior gluteal vessels.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Identify the structures attached to the areas marked 1, 5, and 6 in the tibial plateau below?

options.text: Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus
Anterior horn of medial meniscus, posterior horn of medial meniscus, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments
Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of lateral meniscus
Anterior horn of lateral meniscus, posterior horn of lateral meniscus, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments

questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus
questions.explanation:
The structures attached to areas 1, 5 and 6 are, respectively, the anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and the anterior and posterior horns of the medial meniscus.

The source mnemonic for attachments from anterior to posterior is 'Medial College Ludhiana Ludhiana Medical College': medial meniscus (anterior horn), cruciate ligament (anterior), lateral meniscus (anterior horn), lateral meniscus (posterior horn), medial meniscus (posterior horn), cruciate ligament (posterior).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 19-year-old football player was brought to the hospital after he suffered an injury caused by a lateral blow to the knee joint. MRI revealed an injury to the ligaments commonly referred to as the 'unhappy triad'. Which of the following ligaments are involved?

options.text: Posterior cruciate ligament and lateral meniscus
Anterior cruciate ligament and medial meniscus
Anterior and posterior horns of lateral meniscus

questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior cruciate ligament and medial meniscus
questions.explanation: The unhappy triad of the knee involves the medial meniscus, anterior cruciate ligament and tibial collateral ligament. Among the answer choices, anterior cruciate ligament and medial meniscus are therefore the matching components.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 35-year-old basketball player with knee pain was diagnosed to have coronary ligament strain. Which of the following ligaments is involved?
questions.explanation:
Coronary ligaments are also known as meniscotibial ligaments and refer to the tibial attachment of the medial meniscus.

The medial meniscus is almost semicircular. Its anterior horn attaches to the anterior tibial intercondylar area in front of the anterior cruciate ligament; the posterior horn fixes to the posterior tibial intercondylar area between the attachments of the lateral meniscus and posterior cruciate ligament. These attachments make the medial meniscus relatively fixed and less mobile than the lateral meniscus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Lateral meniscus covers a larger area of the articular surface than medial meniscus
Movements of lateral meniscus is restricted compared to medial meniscus
Peripheral tears of the menisci heal better than central tears
Suprapatellar bursa is an extension of knee joint cavity

questions.correctAnswerText: Movements of lateral meniscus is restricted compared to medial meniscus
questions.explanation:
The false statement is that movement of the lateral meniscus is restricted compared with the medial meniscus. In fact, the medial meniscus is relatively fixed and moves less; the lateral meniscus is more mobile.

Peripheral meniscal zones are vascularized by capillary loops while inner regions are less vascular, so peripheral tears heal better. The suprapatellar bursa is the superior extension of the knee-joint cavity and lies between the femur and suprapatellar part of quadriceps femoris.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is involved in locking of knee?

options.text: Lateral rotation of the femur on tibia during extension
Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during flexion
Lateral rotation of the femur on tibia during flexion
Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during extension

questions.correctAnswerText: Medial rotation of the femur on tibia during extension
questions.explanation:
Locking of the knee is medial rotation of the femur on the tibia during the later stages of extension.

When standing, the knee locks to reduce muscular work needed to maintain posture; the source states vastus medialis is responsible for locking. Unlocking is lateral rotation of the femur on the tibia at the beginning of flexion and is produced by popliteus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which bursae are involved in patients with clergyman's knee and housemaid's knee?

options.text: Prepatellar bursa and infrapatellar bursa respectively
Subcutaneous and deep infrapatellar bursa respectively
Infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively

questions.correctAnswerText: Infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively
questions.explanation:
Clergyman's knee and housemaid's knee result from inflammation of the infrapatellar bursa and prepatellar bursa respectively.

The source lists major lower-limb bursitides: prepatellar bursitis (housemaid's knee), infrapatellar bursitis (clergyman's knee), and trochanteric bursitis above the hip abductor.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 23-year-old cricketer was diagnosed with ligamentum mucosum tear. Range of movements of which of the following joints is affected?
questions.explanation:
Ligamentum mucosum is related to the knee joint and is a plica at the intercondylar notch.

Plicae are embryological remnants of synovial folds. Major knee plicae listed are ligamentum mucosum at the intercondylar notch, suprapatellar plica in the suprapatellar space, and medial plica extending from the infrapatellar fat pad to the medial wall of the knee.

Plica syndrome is a painful knee condition due to thickened/inflamed synovial folds, most commonly involving the medial plica.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient presented to the orthopedics OPD with ankle sprain caused due to hyper inversion of the right foot. Which of the following ligaments is commonly injured?
questions.explanation:
The anterior talofibular ligament is most commonly injured in inversion sprains.

Lateral ankle ligaments likely to be injured with inversion include anterior talofibular ligament (most common), posterior talofibular ligament and calcaneofibular ligament. Medial ligaments more likely injured with eversion include the deltoid (medial collateral) ligament and spring (calcaneonavicular) ligament.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The superficial part of deltoid ligament is attached to all of the following except:
questions.explanation:
The superficial part of the deltoid ligament is attached to all listed bones except the fibula.

The deltoid/medial collateral ligament is a strong triangular band attached to the apex and anterior/posterior borders of the medial malleolus. The source describes two layers. Superficial layer: tibionavicular fibres anteriorly, tibiocalcaneal fibres in the middle, and superficial posterior tibiotalar fibres posteriorly. Deep layer: anterior tibiotalar fibres, tibiocalcaneal fibres in the middle, and deep posterior tibiotalar fibres posteriorly.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which ligament is related to the inferior surface of the structure marked in the image?
questions.explanation:
The marked structure is the head of the talus. The ligament related to its inferior surface is the spring (calcaneonavicular) ligament.

The inferior surface of the talar head has three facets: posterior facet (largest, articulates with sustentaculum tali), anterolateral facet (articulates with the anterior calcaneal facet), and medial facet (related to the spring ligament).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the structure marked in the image?

options.text: It has a triangular fibrocartilaginous facet on which part of the talar head rests
Transection of the ligament leads to adult acquired flat foot
It is a complex of two ligaments
It maintains the medial longitudinal arch of foot

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a complex of two ligaments
questions.explanation:
The marked structure is the spring ligament (plantar calcaneonavicular ligament). The false statement is that it is a complex of two ligaments; the source describes a complex of three ligaments: superomedial calcaneonavicular, medioplantar oblique calcaneonavicular, and inferoplantar longitudinal calcaneonavicular ligaments.

The spring ligament is a thick band connecting the anterior margin of the sustentaculum tali to the plantar surface of the navicular. It stabilizes the medial longitudinal arch and head of talus; disruption causes collapse of the medial longitudinal arch and flat foot.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is Lisfranc's ligament?
questions.explanation:
Lisfranc's ligament is the cuneometatarsal interosseous ligament.

There are three cuneometatarsal interosseous ligaments; Lisfranc's is the strongest. It passes from the lateral surface of the medial cuneiform to the adjacent angle of the second metatarsal. Deformity can cause instability and deformity of the tarsometatarsal joint.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Chopart's ligament is related to which of the following joints?
questions.explanation:
Chopart's ligament is related to both the calcaneocuboid and calcaneonavicular joints.

Chopart's/bifurcate ligament is a strong Y-shaped band with a proximal stem and two distal limbs. The proximal stem attaches to the anterior part of the upper calcaneal surface; the distal limb divides into calcaneocuboid and calcaneonavicular parts.
